o.text: From Classical Persian کِتَابْخَانَه (kitābxāna). By surface analysis, kitab (“book”) + -xana.

Etymology tree
Arabic خَطَّ (ḵaṭṭa)
Arabic خَطّ (ḵaṭṭ)bor.
Azerbaijani xətt
Borrowed from Arabic خَطّ (ḵaṭṭ), from خَطَّ (ḵaṭṭa).
From Russian моне́та (monéta, “coin”), from Polish moneta, from Latin monēta.
From Proto-Turkic *tog-. Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (tugur-, “to give birth to”), Uzbek tugʻmoq (“to give birth to”), Chuvash ту (tu).
From Proto-Turkic *tuy- (“to perceive (by ears or nose), notice”). Cognate with Turkish duymak.

glosses: to attach a spring; to fasten with a spring.
